links.outcome: Exam accuracy with retrieval-augmented generation versus no context
links.effect: GPT-4o improved from 63.1% without context to 73.8% on text-only questions with textbook context; RAG-enabled Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 reached 86.3% and 86.7%.
links.quote: Providing textbook context improved GPT-4o to 73.8% on text-only questions, but still fell short of human trainees.

links.outcome: Refusals by safety filters on exam questions in deployed configuration
links.effect: GPT-5.5 refused a mean of 12.2 questions (7.3%) per iteration due to safety filters.
links.quote: GPT-5.5 achieved 86.7% ± 2.2% (text 88.5%, image 77.0%) but refused a mean of 12.2 questions (7.3%) per iteration due to safety filters.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks newer LLM models (Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5) using retrieval-augmented generation on a medical board examination, evaluating exam performance rather than testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
